documents.title: USF Guidance for Ethical Generative AI Usage
documents.stance_why: The document says "use of genAI tools within university coursework is at the discretion of the instructor and students are expected to follow course- specific policies", so it sets no stance and delegates.
documents.summary: The 2023 Provost principles set out human-centered use, individual responsibility, bias awareness, sourcing, transparency, discipline-specific rules and data protection for generative AI. It sets no coursework rule itself and leaves coursework use to instructors.

units.why: Sets the expectation that units and departments work out their own AI practice: "Individual units and departments are responsible to" explore and share expectations, so the rule-making sits below the university. Actor admin, before-course, P85 because it lets units set their own rules.
units.anchor: Individual units and departments are responsible to
units.frag_start: Individual units and departments are responsible
units.policy: Individual units and departments are responsible to explore the usefulness and limitations of these technologies within their specific contexts and share their experiences and expectations.
units.fit_note: Units are told to explore and share experiences; it does not explicitly say they may set their own rules.

units.why: The document says "our pracIces will evolve, and usage recommendaIons will be updated regularly", which is a statement that the guidance is provisional; this is P54 (revisit regularly), not P84 because it gives no process.
units.anchor: usage recommendaIons will be updated regularly
units.frag_start: As these tools conInue to develop

units.why: Defines the term that sets the scope: "GenAI refers to technologies that can automatically generate new, original content". A definition goes under P61.
units.anchor: GenAI refers to technologies that can automatically generate new, original content

units.why: Principle that AI "should augment - not replace" human strengths, i.e. people stay the thinkers; closest is P32 (stay the primary problem-solver) though addressed to everyone, not just students.
units.anchor: These technologies should augment - not replace - our foundational strengths
units.fit_note: Addressed to all users in general terms, not only students doing assignments.

units.why: Says "Critical thinking, ethical awareness, and human judgment remain essential", a value statement about what must be retained; framework-type preamble so P56.
units.anchor: Critical thinking, ethical awareness, and human judgment remain essential.

units.why: "individuals are responsible for understanding the limits and constraints of the genAI tools they are using" puts responsibility on the user; P29 (own what you use) is the nearest because the text is about responsibility, not about verification.
units.anchor: individuals are responsible for understanding the limits and constraints
units.fit_note: Responsibility is for understanding tool limits rather than for submitted work.

units.why: "Users are responsible for the validity, correctness, and usefulness of the content" makes the user answerable for AI output; P29.
units.anchor: Users are responsible for the validity, correctness, and usefulness of the content

units.why: "Verify facts and" cross-check is an instruction to check AI output because "generative AI models can create incorrect information"; this is P31.
units.anchor: Verify facts and

units.why: States that models "can potentially perpetuate biases" from training data, a concern about harms, so P53 with modality informs.
units.anchor: genAI models can potentially perpetuate biases that exist in their training data

units.why: "Users should proactively work to identify and proactively mitigate any harmful biases" is a duty tied to bias, so P53 rather than P31, since it asks for mitigation, not verification.
units.anchor: Users should proactively work to identify and proactively mitigate any harmful biases
units.fit_note: P53 only names concerns; this one assigns users a duty to mitigate.

units.why: "Users of genAI have an ethical responsibility to respect copyrights, avoid plagiarism" concerns copyright of inputs and outputs, so P52.
units.anchor: ethical responsibility to respect copyrights, avoid plagiarism
units.fit_note: Also folds in avoiding plagiarism.

units.why: The same sentence requires users to "provide proper citations for any generated content", an attribution duty, so P24 (cite AI use) not P52.
units.anchor: provide proper citations for any generated content
units.fit_note: Citation duty is framed as applying to content that builds on others' original work.

units.anchor: Our academic principles require proper acknowledgement of sources, authors, and contributors.
units.fit_note: Refers to sources generally; AI is not named in this sentence.

units.why: Users "should when possible and appropriate disclose content is produced by AI versus human-generated": a hedged disclosure duty, P24 with modality should.
units.anchor: disclose content is produced by AI versus human-generated

units.why: Says disclosure is "especially important for published works, official communications, and student submissions" and links it to instructor permission; P24 for students.
units.anchor: especially important for published works, official communications, and student submissions

units.why: "the university integrates genAI tools into our academic integrity policies" ties AI use to existing integrity rules; P36 is nearest since misuse is handled by integrity processes.
units.anchor: the university integrates genAI tools into our academic integrity policies
units.fit_note: States that AI is within integrity policies; does not say misuse is misconduct.

units.why: "misrepresenting AI-generated work as one’s own goes against our central tenets" bars passing off AI work as your own, so P29 (work submitted must be your own).

units.fit_note: Phrased as a violation of central tenets, no penalty named.

units.uncovered_note: Gives trust and understanding as the reason for disclosing AI use.

units.why: "proactively stay informed about the policies, guidelines, and ethical considerations" is a duty to keep up with relevant field guidance, P102.

units.why: "students are expected to follow course- specific policies" makes students responsible for the rules of each course, P78.
units.anchor: students are expected to follow course- specific policies

units.why: "Users should not share student data, employment data, and other protected or sensitive information" is a data privacy limit, P50.
units.anchor: Users should not share student data, employment data, and other protected or sensitive

units.why: "Users are expected to maintain current USF Technology Policies" binds AI use to existing university policy, P77.
units.anchor: Users are expected to maintain current USF Technology Policies

units.anchor: Users must continue to comply with data privacy regulations including FERPA and HIPAA

units.why: "USF faculty and staff have access to Bing Chat Enterprise Preview which provides a data-protected text-based genAI tool" names an approved tool, P92.
units.anchor: USF faculty and staff have access to Bing Chat Enterprise Preview

units.why: "Current governance structures for institutional data and information will continue to review and explore these technologies" says existing bodies review AI technologies, P65 (institutional review).
units.anchor: Current governance structures for institutional data and information will continue to review
units.fit_note: Review is of the technologies generally, not of specific tools or vendors.

documents.title: Course Guidance (GenAI at USF)
documents.stance_why: The page says "use of genAI tools within university coursework is at the discretion of individual instructors" and "Faculty retain full control over how, or if, AI tools may be used in their course", so it delegates.
documents.summary: Short course-guidance page saying AI use in coursework is up to individual instructors. It recommends discussing integrity with students, being open about instructors’ own AI use, redesigning assessment, and including a clear AI statement in the syllabus.
